reasoning: Major global health authorities and scientific consensus—including the CDC, WHO, and NIH—confirm that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines do not alter, edit, or interact with human DNA in any way. The mRNA from the vaccine enters the cytoplasm of cells to instruct the cell to produce a harmless spike protein that triggers an immune response. It never enters the cell nucleus, where human genomic DNA is located, and is rapidly broken down by normal cellular processes within days. Furthermore, human cells do not possess the necessary reverse transcriptase enzymes required to turn mRNA into DNA. Claims to the contrary stem from fringe websites and misinterpretations of artificial in vitro cell culture studies that do not apply to live human organisms or real-world vaccination.
title: mRNA vaccines alter human DNA
